findings.text: §35 defines "Dropped edges" as "sources exist in the name's history, but no live name holds them", while its "Orphans awaiting retirement" bullet states "a partial transfer leaves the name a dropped edge"; a name that recorded two sources, one now held by a chained successor and one held by no live name, satisfies none of the five population tests literally — not population 2 ("every source the name itself recorded is held by a live name in its own chain" fails on the unheld source), not population 3 (the chain does link it to the holder, so "no chain links the two" fails), not population 4 ("no live name holds them" is false) and not population 5 (a writer did give it a source) — yet the done-when requires "every sourceless live name in exactly one of the five populations"
